summary:
**KEN Moon Explorer** is an interactive scientific platform designed to support the exploration and preliminary assessment of potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole.

The lunar South Pole presents major challenges for future missions, including rugged terrain, permanently shadowed regions, limited sunlight, and communication constraints. Our solution brings together NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topographic data and JPL Horizons ephemerides to help users investigate these conditions through a single web application.

KEN Moon Explorer enables users to explore lunar terrain, estimate local slopes, identify candidate regions, visualize three-dimensional topography, analyze solar illumination and Earth visibility, and compare sites across different mission dates. It also provides interactive mission-planning tools and educational visualizations.

By transforming complex scientific datasets into accessible, actionable insights, our project helps students, researchers, and space enthusiasts better understand the challenges of lunar exploration. Although it does not certify landing-site safety, KEN Moon Explorer demonstrates how open NASA data can support transparent, evidence-based decision-making for future lunar missions.
details: KEN Moon Explorer is an interactive scientific web application designed to support the exploration and preliminary assessment of potential landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole. The platform combines NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topographic data with NASA JPL Horizons ephemerides to analyze lunar terrain, solar illumination, Earth visibility, and mission conditions. Users can select a location, choose a simulation date, and explore how environmental conditions evolve over time. The application provides interactive polar maps, 3D lunar terrain visualizations, local slope assessments, permanently shadowed region indicators, solar elevation measurements, visibility timelines, and tools for comparing potential landing sites. It also includes a scientific decision dashboard, mission-planning features, and a historical atlas of lunar missions. Developed using Python, FastAPI, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, KEN Moon Explorer brings complex scientific information together in a single, accessible platform. Its originality lies in combining geographic analysis, time-dependent astronomical simulations, and mission-oriented decision support while offering both beginner and expert modes. The project addresses key challenges of lunar South Pole exploration, where rugged terrain, limited sunlight, and communication constraints make site selection particularly difficult. By making these conditions easier to visualize and compare, KEN Moon Explorer aims to support scientific understanding, educational exploration, and preliminary mission planning. The application also clearly communicates its limitations: terrain resolution is insufficient to certify landing safety, and geometric visibility does not guarantee power generation or communication reliability. Ultimately, KEN Moon Explorer transforms complex lunar datasets into an interactive tool that helps users explore, understand, and evaluate the Moon’s South Pole.Live application: https://ken-moon-explorer.onrender.com/
